key_insight: The Hotspotters Project found that proactive integrated care was feasible and valued by providers, but low eligibility and enrollment limited conclusions about effectiveness.
clinical_relevance: For complex-needs patients, implementation success may depend more on local patient definitions, recruitment fit, and workflow integration than on the care model alone.
method: Mixed-method process evaluation using the RE-AIM framework
Used questionnaires, routine care data, and semi-structured interviews
Quantitative results were summarized descriptively; interviews were analyzed thematically
evidence_signal: Only 153 of 1403 patients met eligibility criteria and 30 enrolled, so the evidence mainly reflects implementation and adoption rather than treatment effect.
watch_item: The main limitation was very low recruitment due to unexpectedly low acute-care use, which reduced power to assess effectiveness and cost-effectiveness.
paper_title: Lessons learned from a trial on integrated and proactive care for patients with complex needs (Hotspotters project): a process evaluation
